title: Azerbaijan announces the capture of Shusha at the end of a three-day battle
body:
The Battle of Shusha was fought from 6 to 8 November 2020 and was the last decisive engagement of the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War. Azerbaijani forces, mainly special forces, advanced through Jabrayil and Hadrut and then north through forests and mountain passes into Shusha District. They took Chanakchi and part of the Shusha–Lachin road on 4 November, after which Armenian forces closed the road to civilians. Azerbaijani accounts say about 400 special forces troops entered the city on 6 November from four sides and fought building by building, while also blocking the Lachin corridor to stop reinforcements.

On the afternoon of 8 November, President Ilham Aliyev announced that Azerbaijan had taken the city, describing the fighting as an almost hand-to-hand battle. A Defence Ministry video was released on 9 November, and 8 November was later declared Victory Day in Azerbaijan. Armenian authorities denied the capture on 8 and 9 November. The Artsakh presidential office later acknowledged the loss, and Artsakh's president said control had been lost on 7 November. After the ceasefire was signed, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan admitted the loss.

Casualty claims diverged. Azerbaijan officially reported 356 servicemen killed across the entire operation. Pashinyan said more than 300 Armenian servicemen had been killed, based on bodies recovered between 14 and 16 November. Artsakh's president Arayik Harutyunyan said at least 150 had died, with hundreds missing. Azerbaijani sources claimed more than 1,500 Armenian servicemen were killed, a figure Armenia did not confirm.
